pages.title: The Courses of a Hall, as Cut on Its Lintel
pages.by: [DRAFT] Cut in notches down the inner face of a lintel under the Second Ossuary, where the sweepers do not lift their lamps; a tallier who had learned the old letters read it to me one riser at a time, and asked that his number not stand here.
pages.bb:
[DRAFT] [indent][i][color=#c8bfae]The tallier who read this to me from the notches gave the builders the name they cut for themselves, Khurr-Ossat, and would not say it twice. The lowlands say Lintel-Folk. Where his reading failed he said so, and I have kept his failures as he spoke them.[/color][/i][/indent]

For the raising of a hall in her, by us who are of her. The measures, the stuff, and what is cut at every course. Let the one who lays read the course before the course is laid, and not after. Nothing here is to be read after.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]Of the measure[/color][/font_size]

The Knee is the height of the lowest bend of the leg of the one who lays, from the floor he stands on. A riser is one Knee. The small warm ones, when they come, will not be able to walk our stairs. Good. Let them climb.

The Reach is from the shoulder of the one who lays to the end of his longest finger, with the arm straight out. A niche is one body and one Reach over, for the shoulders, which widen as they lie.

The Joint is the measure of counting. A Joint is counted from the bone on this side and again from the bone on that side, because it belongs to both. Two, which is one. Every count in this hall is made in Joints, and every count made in Joints is made twice and comes out once, and the one it comes out to is never the one it went in as.

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]The tallier stopped here and reduced the measures by the Rule, to their roots. He got a figure. He took the roots again and got a different figure. He said the measure does not close, that it is built so, and that a hall measured in it cannot be measured by anyone standing outside it. He then asked me how far I thought we were from the stair.[/color][/i][/indent]

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]Of the stuff[/color][/font_size]

All stuff is bone. Quarry nothing. Cut nothing from her that she has not set down. She sets a bone down when she breathes out; take it then, and only then. A bone taken on the in-breath is still hers, and will go back to her through the wall, and take the wall with it.

The footing is her heel-bones, the great flat ones, laid as they lie. The risers are her shins, split. The courses are her ribs, laid lengthwise, the near ribs first, which are longer than the far. The lintels are the long bones of her arm, and there are only so many of those, and the one who lays is to know the number before he begins and is never to say it.

And the stuff is us. We are of her Bone. We stood up out of it before anything warm had a name for us. What we build with, we are; what we are, we build with. There is no difference in the specification between the course and the one who lays it, and none is to be introduced.

[font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]Of what is done at every course[/color][/font_size]

She breathes in. We cut. She breathes out. We count the Joints the out-breath has let us lay. Then one of us lies down in the niche of that course, facing the stair, and the course is set on him, and his Joints are added to the count of the course, twice, as is proper. Then the notches are cut in the lintel of the course, one for each Joint laid, on the in-breath, so that the count is hers and not ours. Then we watch.

This is the whole of the rite. There is no other. A hall is not finished by the laying but by the lying down, and a hall in which nobody lies is a heap.

[center][color=#8c6a37]❧[/color][/center]

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The footing[/color][/font_size]
Measure: the hall's width is thirty-six Joints, which are eighteen, which are not nine. Stuff: her heels, unsplit. Said: nothing. The footing is laid in the first out-breath and the floor is sloped toward the pillar by one Knee in a hundred Reach, so that what is set down in the hall goes to the middle of its own accord. Four lie down in the footing, one at each corner, facing in.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The first course, the shins[/color][/font_size]
Measure: one Knee high, round the whole hall. Stuff: her shins, split along the grain, the marrow left in. Said, by the one who lies down: [i]I am counted.[/i] Said, by the rest: [i]Twice.[/i] The stair begins in this course. Cut the risers one Knee, every one. Cut no riser higher, and no riser lower, and cut them in the number the out-breath allows and not one more, because a stair with a riser cut on the in-breath has a step on the way down that is not there on the way up.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The second course, the ribs[/color][/font_size]
Measure: one Reach high. Stuff: the near ribs. Said: the count of the first course, aloud, by all, in Joints, twice, and the two figures compared, and the difference between them cut into the lintel as a notch standing apart. Nine lie down in this course, in the long niches, facing the stair.

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]The notch that stands apart is cut deeper than the others on every lintel the tallier has read. He says the difference is never the same twice and is never nothing.[/color][/i][/indent]

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The third course, the far ribs[/color][/font_size]
As the second, in the far ribs, which are shorter, so the hall closes in as it rises and the one who stands in it looks up along a throat. Said: nothing. Those who lie down in this course lie with their mouths open. The specification does not say why. The specification was cut by those who lie in it and they are still saying it.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The fourth course, the pillar[/color][/font_size]
The pillar stands where the floor arrives. Stuff: one bone, whole, which she sets down once in a hall's raising, and the one who lays is to wait for it, through as many breaths as it takes, and is to do nothing else, and is to let the warm ones come in and sit down and go away again before he moves. The script is cut on the pillar in rings, with no first line, so that it cannot be read by beginning. Measure: the pillar is one Joint high. The tallier is not to measure it.

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]I did not measure it. I asked the tallier to tell me how a pillar four men high is one Joint and he said that it is one Joint and that the hall is inside it, and I did not ask again.[/color][/i][/indent]

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The fifth course, the shoulders[/color][/font_size]
Measure: the hall's width at this height is the hall's width at the footing, which is a greater width than it was, and the lintel of this course is cut to the greater. Stuff: the blades of her shoulders, which are flat and take the notches well. Said: the count of all the courses beneath, which does not agree with itself, and is cut as it does not agree.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The sixth course, the jaw[/color][/font_size]
This is the course of the door. The door is the mouth of the hall and is cut facing in, so that the mouth is kept by what it holds. Measure: the mouth is one Reach wide and one Reach high and will admit one of us lying down and two of the warm ones standing, and they will go in and out of it for an age and not know what they are going in and out of. Stuff: her jaw, the lower, which hinges. Everyone left lies down in this course. The last of us to lie down lies across the sill, under the floor of the door, and the warm ones will walk on him, and he is to count them, twice.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The seventh course, the lintel of the mouth[/color][/font_size]
Measure: [ … ]. Stuff: the last long bone of her arm, which has been dressed and lies ready on the floor of the lowest hall, one Reach from the pillar. Said: nothing, for the count is closed and there is nobody to say it. This course is laid when she breathes in and does not breathe out. It closes the mouth. It is the only course in the specification laid on the in-breath, because it is the course that is laid when there is no out-breath to follow.

She has not breathed in.

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]The notches end here. The dressed bone lies where the specification says it lies, too long for any nine brothers to lift, and the sweepers do not sweep round it. The Order's gate stands in the sixth course. I have walked through it in and out for nine winters, and so has every brother, and the Order's chronicle says the Order cut it. The tallier read me the last notch, the one standing apart, and said that it was fresh, and that he had read this lintel before and it had not been there. He has asked to be moved to the sweeping. They have not moved him. He says the step on the Gate Stair that is there on the way down is not a step. He says it is a sill.[/color][/i][/indent]

[right][i][color=#c9974a]— [two bones meeting at a joint, cut deeper than any notch, and under it a row of notches the tallier would not count aloud][/color][/i][/right]
